note: Practice pack: 11+ vocabulary tasks with fixed answers. Generic content - contains no personal information.

tasks.prompt: Word detective! Which ONE word fits BOTH clues: 'a harbour for ships' AND 'the left side of a boat'?
tasks.teach: Port is the harbour AND the boat's left side. One word, two jobs — English loves a doubler.
The knight rescued the villagers from their plight — their sticky situation.

tasks.prompt: Three of these pull you closer. Which one pushes you away?
tasks.teach: Entice, tempt and attract are magnets — deter is the force field that stops you.
The comma tucks INSIDE the speech marks, right after the last word spoken — then a little 'said'.

tasks.prompt: Where does the question mark go?
tasks.teach: If the SPOKEN words ask a question, the ? goes inside the speech marks — and you don't need a comma as well.
A shout keeps its ! INSIDE the speech marks, hugging the words that are shouted.

tasks.prompt: When the 'she said' comes FIRST, which is correct?
tasks.teach: When the 'she said' comes first, pop a comma before the speech marks, then start the talking with a capital letter.

tasks.prompt: The robot lifted ___ arm. (the arm belonging to it)
tasks.teach: 'Its' with no apostrophe means 'belonging to it'. 'It's' is ONLY ever short for 'it is'.

tasks.prompt: ___ going to love this level! (you are)
tasks.teach: 'You're' is short for 'you are'. 'Your' means belonging to you, like 'your book'.

tasks.prompt: The children grabbed ___ coats. (the coats belonging to them)
tasks.teach: 'Their' = belonging to them. 'There' = a place (over there). 'They're' = they are.

tasks.prompt: It is ___ hot to play outside. (more than enough)
tasks.teach: 'Too' with two O's means 'more than enough' or 'also'. 'To' points somewhere, like 'to school'.

tasks.prompt: More than one daisy — which spelling?
tasks.teach: When a word ends in 'y', swap the y for 'ies': daisy→daisies, story→stories, party→parties.

tasks.prompt: Fix this sentence: The text say she is tired.
tasks.answer: The text says she is tired.
tasks.teach: One person doing something now needs 's' on the verb: the text SAYS, she RUNS, he PLAYS.

options: Although the robot is clever, it needs charging.
Although, the robot is clever, it needs charging.
Although the robot is clever it needs charging.
Although, the robot is clever it needs charging.
tasks.answer: Although the robot is clever, it needs charging.
tasks.teach: 'Although' hugs its whole idea first — the comma waits until that idea finishes, not straight after 'although'.

tasks.prompt: Sentence detective! Which one is a COMPLETE sentence?
options: The firebird soared into the golden sky.
tasks.answer: The firebird soared into the golden sky.
tasks.teach: A whole sentence needs someone AND what they do. 'Scrambling away…' — who? doing what? Finish the thought!
'Every' likes its own space: every night, every day, every time — always two words.
